history.sg_progress: The task force of the Procurement Network of the High-level Committee on Management on the revision of the model policy framework for handling allegations of vendors having engaged in proscribed practices has finalized a draft revision of the document, which is currently under review by participating organizations. The framework defines a common, harmonized approach and enables United Nations system organizations to share information based on decisions taken by their respective sanctions boards. The sanctions are recorded in the shared United Nations Global Marketplace application. In addition, the Secretariat has issued a new standard operating procedure for the Vendor Review Committee, which includes provisions for the implementation of the mutual recognition principle. Following the issuance of the model policy framework, the Secretariat will encourage further cooperation among the respective sanctions boards.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration strengthen the coordination on vendor sanctions with other agencies, funds and programmes of the United Nations system, with the objective of assessing the feasibility and benefits of establishing, in the medium term, a joint vendor committee to harmonize procedures and actions taken.
history.administration_response: The Administration considers this recommendation to be implemented. As recommended by the Board, the Administration has strengthened coordination with other agencies, funds and programmes by participating in discussions and providing detailed feedback on the revised model policy framework for vendor sanction procedures. Although the revised model policy framework has not been formally adopted, the draft language (as shared before) clearly indicates a concerted effort to seek stronger coordination and harmonization on vendor sanctions. As part of this review process, an assessment has also been conducted regarding the feasibility of establishing a joint vendor committee, thereby fulfilling the second part of the recommendation. Any further action and decisions are beyond the Administration’s control. Given that the Administration has already provided its input to the system- wide effort, it respectfully requests the closure of this recommendation.
history.board_assessment: The Board notes the progress made in updating the model policy framework. The Board also notes that the adoption of the revised model policy framework has been pushed forward by the Secretariat, and that the subject has been placed on the agenda of the October 2025 session of the Procurement Network of the High-level Committee on Management. Given that the Secretariat is not solely responsible for the adoption of the model policy framework, the Board considers the recommendation to be implemented.
